task: Single authorized option-C lazy per-pattern preparation experiment, PR5983 / issue6465
decision: NO_GO: stop top-k admission implementation and measurement; no further iteration without root evaluation
decision_basis: Allocation traffic is reduced, but both drained fixtures remain materially slower than disabled fallback with disjoint measured ranges. Base-k512, overlay-k1 and prefix128-overlay also show small slowdowns versus dc with disjoint within-process ranges; intermittent-overlay is slower but ranges overlap. All cases are retained without retiming. This is a local diagnostic engineering result, not a canonical benchmark or an independent review.

implementation: Resolve probe metadata eagerly, retain each scan/vector only at first use in the original pattern order, then reuse it. The original exact scan cardinality and actual-sort checks precede use of that probe. A successful row necessarily visits every probe. The old cap formula, block boundaries/extension, failure counter, shape, budget, view and fanout checks remain. If any probe remains unvisited at an otherwise empty completion, conservatively fall back. Main bind_join is byte-identical. No point scout, storage API or new threshold was introduced.
correctness_argument: Before a row can be emitted, every pattern has been prepared and every original eligibility/probe check has passed. A late selective pattern still forces fallback even if the best candidate would match it.
A failed pattern remains a conjunction rejection in the same pattern order; later work cannot make that candidate match. No output columns or result rows are emitted for partial candidates.

The walk uses exactly the existing logical direction, geometric end/visited_to accounting, full tie extension and failure budget. No scout restarts, skipped block-width accounting or smaller new cutoff.

Unvisited static exclusions cannot authorize a new empty indexed result. Budgeted/unsupported views, repeated variables, unsupported sort/datatype shapes and multi-valued variable probes remain on the existing evaluator.

other_observations: Versus dc: base-k512 median+1.7%, overlay-k1+5.0%, prefix128-overlay+2.3%, all with disjoint repetition ranges; intermittent-overlay+5.3% has overlapping ranges. Tie base/overlay remain1.14x/1.16x disabled medians, with base ranges overlapping and overlay disjoint. First base-k1 disabled/main timing ratio is1.82 despite identical allocation metrics: process/host variability prevents precise causal attribution or universal speedup claims.

Peaks are unchanged because the unused preparation was already freed before fallback peak. Favorable new/eager allocation metrics are equal. Against dc, admitted fixtures retain a144-byte increase from larger probe metadata; no claim of globally identical allocation totals.
memory_limits: Requested bytes are allocation traffic (including full new realloc sizes), not simultaneous live memory. peak_live_delta is requested live heap above query baseline, excluding allocator metadata, stack, mappings and allocator-internal transient realloc peaks. macOS getrusage RSS is cumulative process high-water, recorded after setup/warmup/query; cannot isolate a resettable query-only RSS peak. Flat cumulative RSS does not imply zero query memory.
